title: Stoicism
examples: What is the difference between what I can control and what I cannot?
Can Stoicism help me feel less stressed about grades?
Who was Marcus Aurelius and why should I care?

explain.say: Stoicism teaches us about control in our lives. You must learn to separate what is up to you and what is not.
We can control our thoughts and our reactions to things. We cannot control external events happening around us.
Epictetus was a former slave who taught these ideas. He said we should focus only on our own will.
Marcus Aurelius was a Roman Emperor who wrote reflections. He reminded himself to live virtuously each day.
A real-life example is getting a bad grade on a test. You cannot control the test difficulty, but you can control how you study next time.
A common mistake is blaming others for our feelings. Remember, your judgment is what causes your emotional response, not the event itself.

faq.q: If I cannot control what others think of me, does that mean I should just stop caring?
faq.a: No, it means you should stop letting their opinions dictate your inner peace. You can still care about people while accepting their freedom to disagree.
asks: How do I stop worrying about what people think?
Should I ignore everything people say?

faq.q: Is Stoicism about being emotionless or cold?
faq.a: Not at all. It is about managing strong emotions so they do not control your rational actions. It teaches you to feel deeply but respond wisely.
asks: Does Stoicism mean I can't feel sad?

faq.q: What exactly does 'virtue' mean in this philosophy?
faq.a: Virtue generally means living according to reason and developing strong moral character. Key virtues include wisdom, justice, courage, and temperance.
asks: Is virtue the most important thing?

faq.q: Did Epictetus teach this in a formal university setting?
faq.a: No, he taught these principles through personal experience and dialogue. His teachings were practical guides for daily life.

faq.q: Does Stoicism only apply to big problems, like wars or disasters?
faq.a: No, it applies to small daily frustrations too. It helps you handle minor annoyances, like traffic or slow service, with calm.
asks: Can this help with small things?

facts: Stoicism emphasizes that virtue is the only true good.
The core idea is distinguishing between what is 'up to us' and what is not.
Epictetus taught that our judgments cause our emotions.
Marcus Aurelius advised accepting fate with reason.

quiz.say: If you study hard for a test but still perform poorly, what should your focus be?

options.show: Blaming the teacher for unclear questions.
options.say: Blaming the teacher for unclear questions.

quiz.why: The correct answer focuses on the effort, which is within your control, not the grade, which is influenced by many factors.

wrong.0: This blames an external person and does not help you change your study habits.
wrong.1: This is an action of giving up control and accepting defeat.
wrong.2: Worrying about the future is an external event you cannot control right now.

quiz.say: Which concept suggests that our feelings come from how we judge things?
quiz.why: This shows that the internal thought process, the judgment, is the root cause of the emotional reaction.

wrong.0: The event is just the trigger; it is not the judgment that causes the feeling.
wrong.1: While people act, your reaction to their actions is what you control.
wrong.2: The physical reaction is the result, not the cause, of the emotional response.

quiz.say: A student gets criticized by a friend. According to Stoicism, what is the best response?

options.show: Accept the criticism as an opinion.
options.say: Accept the criticism as an opinion.

quiz.why: Accepting it as an opinion means you acknowledge it exists but refuse to let it damage your inner peace.

wrong.1: Anger is a strong emotional reaction that is based on resisting what is outside your control.
wrong.2: While you control your response, ignoring them entirely might lose a chance to learn something.
wrong.3: Defending yourself often involves arguing about what others think, which is outside your control.
